svg.title: The accounting duty survived the amendment
svg.desc: Original Final Vestige Studios three-panel legal chronology. In 1984 Louisiana ordered a return of qualifying Bohemia Spillway property and an accounting of its revenues. In 1985 the state altered distribution procedures but retained the accounting requirement. In 1996 a Louisiana appellate court reversed a procedural dismissal of claims to royalties from 1984 until title deeds were transferred. The ruling was not a final payment judgment.
svg.metadata: Creator: Final Vestige Studios Editorial Research. Created: 2026-11-16. Rights: Copyright (c) 2026 Final Vestige Studios, all rights reserved. Editorial explanatory diagram, not a historical photograph, original court document, or AI-generated reconstruction. Evidence: Haspel & Davis v. Bd. of Levee Commissioners, 680 So.2d 159 (La. Ct. App. September 4, 1996), text mirrored at https://openjurist.org/680/so2d/159/haspel-davis-v-bd-of-levee-com-rs and https://hallapproved.com/la/cases/appeals/1996/1634298/. The court reproduces and construes Act 233 of 1984 and Act 819 of 1985. Caption: A procedural ruling preserved a claim to mineral royalties; it did not document their payment. Suggested alt: Three-part chronology: 1984 property return and accounting mandate; 1985 distribution procedures changed while accounting requirement remained; 1996 court revived pre-deed royalty claims but ordered no claimant payment.
svg.text: No recipient ledger is established by this ruling.
FINAL VESTIGE STUDIOS / ORIGINAL EVIDENCE DIAGRAM / 2026
